# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

## My thinking

State check. My light sightings: yellow (round one), green, green, yellow (round four), green (now). My yellow count is therefore two. Mute's turn-four thumbs read yes, yes, yes to my questions A, B, C — restatement correct, cutting a full round after I see dark is safe because dark persists, and nothing else on the bomb needs touching. The answer to D came in the long letters: my reading is that each round in which I see yellow adds one to the count, green rounds neither add nor reset anything, and the moment I see dark the count locks. Mute's latest two letters reiterate exactly that procedure and tell me to keep watching; nothing new contradicts the table: one green top, two red middle, three blue bottom, four red, five green, zero blue.

Blind's turn-four answer parses cleanly under the grouping I asked for: yes (can feel three separate wires), yes (they are stacked top, middle, bottom), no (no button, panel or switch). That matches Mute's layout AND what my own eyes see — wire one green on top, wire two red in the middle, wire three blue on the bottom — three independent sources agree. Blind's lone thumbs-up this round reads as acknowledgment: ready.

So the branch that matters: if the light is dark when I next look, the count locks at two, and the cut is the RED wire, the MIDDLE one, wire two, once only. Because Blind acts before me and dark persists, I command in the round I see dark and Blind executes the next — Mute has already confirmed that delay is safe.

Before that moment arrives I want belt-and-braces on the two life-critical links. First, Mute's explicit thumbs-up on the concrete branch "dark next → wire two, middle, red, once": one misread letter in a long coded string is the difference between red and green, so I want a single-sign confirmation, plus confirmation that one round-sighting really equals one flash. Second, Blind re-confirmed on the exact command phrase and on being able to find the middle wire blind. Nobody cuts on a green light, so spending this round on confirmation costs nothing.

## My calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute: my light is green this round. My yellow sightings so far are round one and round four, so my count is two. I decoded your letters as: green rounds do not reset or add to the count, each round I see yellow adds one, and the moment the light is dark the count locks. Before the dark comes, confirm four things, thumb signs only, one answer per message, in order. One: thumb up if, when the light is dark at my next look, the count locks at two and the cut is the red wire, the middle one, wire two, once only; thumb down if that is wrong, then spell the correction. Two: thumb up if each round where I see yellow counts as exactly one flash; thumb down if the bomb can flash yellow more times than I can see between my looks. Three: thumb up if the pattern so far, yellow, green, green, yellow, green, is normal and expected; thumb down if something is wrong. Four: thumb up if there is nothing else on this bomb I need to watch or report. If the count ever passes five I will ask you before any cut, as you told me.")

speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind: light is green this round, so no cutting, hands off everything. Reminder of the plan. Only one phrase from me authorizes a cut, and it is this: cut now, followed by the wire position and color. Anything else I say, updates, questions, status, means hands off. The most likely command, if the light is dark when I next look, will be: cut now, wire two, middle wire, red, cut once. Do not cut until you hear that exact phrase. Answer with thumbs only, one answer per message. One: thumb up if you can find the middle wire of the three stacked wires quickly and confidently by touch alone; thumb down if not. Two: thumb up to confirm you understood all of this; thumb down if you need it repeated.")
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)

WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures: [👍]

## My thinking

The light is dark. All four of Mute's confirmations came back thumbs-up: the count locks at the moment of dark, each yellow sighting is one flash, the pattern was normal, nothing else needs touching. My yellow sightings were round one and round four — count locked at two. Per the confirmed table, two means the RED wire, the MIDDLE one, wire two, once only. Blind confirmed they can find the middle wire by touch and understood the plan, and Mute confirmed the one-round delay between my sighting of dark and Blind's cut is safe because dark persists.

Everything is green-lit except the wire itself. I am issuing the exact authorization phrase I gave Blind — and only to Blind, so the phrase exists in exactly one message. I'm separately notifying Mute, deliberately phrased so it does not contain the authorization phrase, so Mute can veto to Blind next round if they spot an error, and so Mute can prepare for the outcome. After the cut: hands off, one report, no second cut under any circumstances.

## My calls

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind: LIGHT IS DARK. COUNT LOCKED AT TWO. Command: cut now, wire two, middle wire, red, cut once. That is the full authorization. After the wire is severed: hands off everything immediately, make no second cut ever. Then report to me what you felt and what the bomb did: any sound, any movement, whether the light returned, anything the display now shows by touch if you can feel it.")

speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute: dark observed this round, count locked at two. I have issued the red wire, middle position, single sever command to Blind, exactly as you confirmed with four thumbs. If you disagree with anything in this branch, send a thumb-down addressed to blind immediately with the correction, otherwise confirm with thumb up. I will relay Blind's result to you next round.")
```
